name: robots.txt and Sitemap Checker
title: robots.txt Tester and XML Sitemap Checker
description: Test whether a URL is allowed for Googlebot, GPTBot or any user agent under a robots.txt file, and check an XML sitemap for duplicates, relative URLs and bad dates. Runs in your browser.
card: Test robots.txt rules for any bot and validate XML sitemaps.
lede: Paste a robots.txt file to test any path for any crawler, or paste a sitemap to find duplicates, relative URLs and invalid dates.
answer_q: How do I check if robots.txt blocks a page?
answer: Find the group for the crawler's user agent (or the * group if there is none), then apply the longest matching Allow or Disallow rule; a tie goes to Allow. Paste the file here, type the bot and path, and the tool applies those rules for you.
steps: Paste the robots.txt content, or enter the site and press Fetch if the site allows cross-site reads.
Type the user agent, for example `Googlebot` or `GPTBot`.
Type a path or full URL to test.
Read the verdict and the rule that decided it.
Switch to the Sitemap tab to paste and check your sitemap XML.

examples.title: Longest match wins
examples.output: ALLOWED. The longest matching rule is Allow: /admin/public/

p: This tool asks for the file straight from your browser and never sends your request through a server. Browsers only let one site read another site's files when that site allows it (CORS), and most do not for robots.txt. When that happens, open the file in a new tab, copy it, and paste it in.

faq.q: Does Disallow remove a page from Google?
faq.a: No. Disallow stops crawling, but a blocked URL can still be indexed from links. To keep a page out of results, allow crawling and add a noindex tag.

faq.q: How do I block AI crawlers?
faq.a: Add a group for each crawler you want to block, for example `User-agent: GPTBot` followed by `Disallow: /`. Check each AI company's documentation for its crawler names.

faq.q: What does a $ at the end of a rule mean?
faq.a: It anchors the rule to the end of the URL. `Disallow: /*.pdf$` blocks URLs ending in .pdf but not /file.pdf?download=1.

faq.q: How big can a sitemap be?
faq.a: The sitemaps.org protocol allows up to 50,000 URLs and 50 MB uncompressed per file. Larger sites split into several sitemaps listed in a sitemap index.
